scholarships.title: Invest Your Talent in Italy (IYT) — MAECI / ICE / Uni-Italia scholarship programme
scholarships.official_source: Ministero degli Affari Esteri e della Cooperazione Internazionale (MAECI) — Directorate General for Growth and Export Promotion, with ICE and Uni-Italia

existing.funding_period: per academic year (9 months of study), paid quarterly
existing.description: Invest Your Talent in Italy is a MAECI scholarship programme run with the ICE Agency and Uni-Italia that pays a nine-month scholarship to foreign students from 22 partner countries to attend a Master's or Postgraduate course at a participating Italian university, combined with a compulsory internship at an Italian company or professional association. Courses are taught entirely in English, and the programme includes study of Italian language and culture plus a mandatory gender-equality and anti-gender-violence seminar or module. The winner receives an annual scholarship of EUR 10,800, paid quarterly into an Italian bank account in the holder's name, and is exempt from enrolment fees and university contributions, but must still pay the regional right-to-education tax, stamp duty, accident and civil liability insurance and health insurance. The scholarship explicitly does not cover travel expenses and does not include accommodation, and the recipient must independently arrange health insurance.
eligibility: Citizens of Argentina, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Bangladesh, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Egypt, Ethiopia, Ghana, India, Indonesia, Iran, Kazakhstan, Mexico, Mongolia, Paraguay, Peru, People's Republic of China, Tunisia, Türkiye, Uruguay or Vietnam, permanently resident in that country
Hold an academic qualification valid for enrolment in a Master's/Postgraduate degree programme at the chosen institution; students who are about to graduate are not eligible

Have submitted, following each university's own procedures, an application for pre-admission to a course included in the IYT programme; no exceptions are made for courses or universities not in the project
May apply for only one course (with a second, binding preference permitted for courses with limited enrolment)
Born on or after 1 January 2000, except applicants for scholarship renewal
English language proficiency certified from level B2 of the Common European Framework of Reference
Knowledge of Italian certified, or a declaration of commitment to attend a classroom or self-study Italian course before departure
Not currently studying at an Italian university and not holding an Italian university degree
existing.eligibility_summary: Citizens permanently resident in one of 22 partner countries, born on or after 1 January 2000, holding a qualification valid for enrolment in an IYT Master's or Postgraduate course, and not already studying at or graduated from an Italian university.
benefits: Nine months of study starting 1 October 2026 for the 2026-2027 academic year
Compulsory internship in an Italian company or professional association
Italian language and culture study integrated into the programme

Tax exemption under Article 3, paragraph 3, letter d-ter of the Consolidated Income Tax Law for IRPEF purposes, since sums paid as scholarships by the Italian Government to foreign citizens under international agreements are exempt

Additional university scholarships ('Borse Ateneo') offered by six participating universities: Università di Parma, Università degli Studi di Firenze, Università degli Studi di Bergamo, Università degli Studi della Tuscia, Università Ca' Foscari Venezia, Università degli Studi di Brescia
A reserved quota of IYT scholarships for Architecture and Design courses for applicants from India, Indonesia, Turkey, Brazil and Ethiopia
coverage: Annual scholarship of EUR 10,800 paid quarterly into an Italian bank account held in the scholar's name
Exemption from enrolment fees and university contributions at the participating institution
Study of Italian language and culture within the programme
Compulsory internship at an Italian company or professional association representative of the region
Seminar or training module on gender equality and the fight against gender-based violence in the academic curriculum
requirements: Applications must be submitted exclusively online through the programme's My-App registration page
Online applications submitted between 20 April 2026 and 11 May 2026 at 6:00pm Italian time for the 11th edition
Names and surnames must be entered exactly as they appear on the passport
Multiple applications using different email addresses are strictly prohibited and will be rejected
The scholarship only covers attendance at courses in Italy; participation in university international mobility programmes, company internships abroad and thesis research abroad are not possible
The scholarship is subject to prior review of legality by the Court of Auditors, so the actual award depends on the positive outcome of those checks
Course listings are published on the basis of a written undertaking by the relevant Rector, subject to withdrawal within 60 days if the university's governing bodies do not ratify participation
documents: Certificate of completed exams for the qualification valid for enrolment in the Master's/University Master's programme (final transcript), including the degree mark/CGPA. If the degree has been completed but the certificate not yet issued, a certificate/statement from the university on headed paper, dated and signed by an official of the secretary's office, certifying the programme is complete and the degree certificate is awaited

Certification of English language proficiency from level B2 CEFR (Cambridge, IELTS, TOEFL iBT, ISE Digital – Trinity College, ISE Paper – Trinity College, PTE, Linguaskill, ESOL, TOEIC covering listening, reading, speaking, writing). Candidates who obtained a university degree at the end of a degree course taught in English may submit a university certificate attesting English as the language of instruction, accepted as proof of level C1

Certification of knowledge of the Italian language issued by the institution where the training was undertaken, or a declaration of commitment to attend a classroom or self-study Italian course before departure

A video of no longer than 59 seconds explaining reasons for wanting to study in Italy, professional goals, and how the candidate would benefit from an internship in an Italian company; may be filmed in English or Italian, with Italian viewed positively in evaluation
A Curriculum vitae et studiorum, maximum one page
A valid passport; citizens with dual nationality (Italian and foreign) must upload both passports, and I.R.E. (Italian Resident Abroad) status does not give rise to any reservations
existing.english_requirement: Courses are taught entirely in English. Applicants must attach certification of English language proficiency from level B2 of the Common European Framework of Reference (Cambridge, IELTS, TOEFL iBT, ISE Digital – Trinity College, ISE Paper – Trinity College, PTE, Linguaskill, ESOL, TOEIC covering listening, reading, speaking, writing). Candidates who obtained a university degree at the end of a degree course taught in English may submit a university certificate attesting that English was the language of instruction, accepted as proof of level C1. A separate requirement exists for Italian: certification issued by the institution where the training was undertaken, or a declaration of commitment to attend a classroom or self-study Italian course before departure; Italian certification is not mandatory but contributes to the evaluation score.
application_method: Apply for pre-admission to a chosen IYT course directly with that university, following the university's own procedures, within the deadlines set by the Technical Committee
Register on the IYT portal (My-App) using name and surname exactly as printed on the passport

Upload the required documents: final transcript with CGPA (or the dated and signed university statement if the certificate is pending), English proficiency certification from B2, Italian certification or commitment declaration, a video of no longer than 59 seconds, a one-page CV, and a valid passport
Submit the application online during the published call window
Await the Technical Committee's comparative evaluation; successful candidates are informed by email to the registration address
existing.selection_notes: Examination and evaluation of applications is carried out by the Technical Committee of the IYT Program (MAECI, ICE and Uni-Italia), which may use an ad hoc commission. Scholarships are allocated in quotas defined for each country and awarded on the basis of a comparative evaluation of the applications against the requirements in Articles 3 and 5 of the call. The Design Scholarship quota is allocated using specially drawn-up rankings that take into account the order of preference for courses given by the student, as is the Borse Ateneo quota.
existing.best_fit: Students aged 25 or under (born on or after 1 January 2000) who hold a qualification valid for enrolment in a participating Italian Master's or Postgraduate course, permanently resident in one of the 22 listed partner countries, and not already studying at or graduated from an Italian university.
existing.notes: Renewable: IYT scholarship holders may apply to continue the second year of the Master's by uploading a university certificate of exams taken (CFU), a certificate of attendance for an Italian language course (and, for the 11th edition holders, an internship project) by 20 July 2027; renewal and fee exemption for the second year are conditional on achieving 30 credits by 20 July 2027 and verified regular attendance of the university's Italian language course. All scholarship recipients must complete the paperwork for the start of their internship by 20 January 2027. Incompatible: the IYT scholarship cannot be combined with any other scholarship or financial benefit from the Italian Government or any public institution (e.g. Erasmus+), including scholarships offered by Italian regions under regional education programmes. Must fund separately: the scholarship does not cover travel expenses and does not include accommodation, and the recipient must independently arrange health insurance covering illness and accidents in Italy. Not covered even after fee waiver: regional tax for the Right to Education, stamp duty, accident and/or civil liability insurance costs, and health insurance. Restrictions on mobility: the scholarship only covers attendance at courses in Italy. Award is conditional on the positive outcome of the Court of Auditors legality review.
existing.duration: 9 months of study, starting 1 October 2026 for the 2026-2027 academic year
existing.application_period: The 11th edition ran 20 April 2026 to 11 May 2026 at 6:00pm Italian time and is closed, with 1634 applications received, 982 eligible and 211 scholarships awarded. The official site carries the banner 'NEW APPLICATION OPENS 2027!' / 'IL NUOVO BANDO APRE NEL 2027!', so the next edition is announced but no opening date, closing date or application window has been published.
existing.deadline_display: The 11th edition (academic year 2026-2027) call was open from 20 April 2026 and closed at 6:00pm Italian time on 11 May 2026. The official programme site announces that the new call opens in 2027 (the 12th edition).

scholarships.title: Max Weber Fellowships — European University Institute Max Weber Programme for Postdoctoral Studies
scholarships.official_source: European University Institute (EUI) — Max Weber Programme for Postdoctoral Studies

existing.description: The Max Weber Programme is the postdoctoral programme of the European University Institute, an intergovernmental research institute of the European Union based at Badia Fiesolana near Florence. It awards 1- and 2-year fellowships of EUR 2,500 per month to researchers within five years of completing their PhD, from any nationality. A cohort typically comprises around 65 Fellows distributed across the EUI academic units, and the annual acceptance rate is stated to be under 2%. The current call is for a 1 September 2027 start with an application deadline of 16 October 2026.
eligibility: Within 5 years from the completion of the PhD
Open to applicants from anywhere in the world, regardless of nationality
Preference is given to applicants who have only just completed their doctorate and have not had a postdoctoral fellowship before
Applicants from the EUI's listed Widening countries are encouraged to apply
existing.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be within five years of completing their PhD and must not have held a postdoctoral fellowship before; there is no nationality restriction.
benefits: Personal mission and research fund of EUR 1,500
Research facilities and library access at Badia Fiesolana
In year two, qualifying Fellows may apply for a 12-month part-time assistant professor contract at level ASSPR/6/3, with net remuneration of approximately EUR 850 in addition to the monthly grant
coverage: Personal mission and research fund of EUR 1,500
requirements: Doctoral thesis completed no more than five years before the application
Research proposal for the postdoctoral project
application_method: Online application through the EUI OSIRIS portal (apply.eui.eu), process code MWP-APPLY
Second-stage interviews are conducted at the EUI
existing.selection_notes: The Programme is highly selective, with an annual acceptance rate of under 2%. The EUI additionally runs country- and foundation-funded special grants (Finland, Germany, Greece, Poland, Japan) and one IHEID Geneva extension place; eligible applicants are considered for these automatically.
existing.best_fit: Early-career researchers in history, law, economics, political and social sciences and transnational governance who completed their doctorate within the last five years.
existing.notes: Applicants are not required to have a teaching or research contract at the EUI; the award itself is the funding instrument. Additional government- and foundation-funded special grants are advertised under the programme's Information for Applicants tab and vary from year to year.
existing.duration: 1 year, or 2 years depending on the hosting academic unit; a third year only in exceptional cases
